domain_specific.reason: Focused on vertical-specific problems (healthcare, gaming, agriculture, manufacturing) not applicable to Vitrina's SMB agency mission
examples: Healthcare diagnosis agents (HIPAA concerns, domain expertise required)
Smart farming assistant (agriculture-specific data, not SMB general use)
Gaming AI companions (gaming domain, no business value for SMB)
Energy forecasting agents (specialized energy sector)

research_and_toy_projects.reason: Proof-of-concept, experimental, or educational; not production-ready for Vitrina
examples: Experimental LLM explorations (academic papers without runnable code)
Tutorial agents (designed to teach, not for production use)
Prototype implementations (unclear if maintained or functional)

single_task_agents.reason: Solve one narrow problem; not modular or orchestrable; Vitrina needs composable agents
examples: Stock price checker (narrow data retrieval, no business workflow)
Weather agent (utility only)
Trivia bot (no business application)
Single-API wrappers (not generalizable)

framework_locked.reason: Tightly coupled to specific LLM provider, framework, or proprietary API; not transferable to Vitrina architecture
examples: Hugging Face model-specific agents (locked to HF ecosystem)
Brand-specific integration agents (Salesforce, Zendesk proprietary API)
Experiment-only code (not designed for portability)

license_unverified.reason: No clear LICENSE or proprietary; cannot verify reusability or commercial use rights
examples: Repositories without LICENSE file
Ambiguous dual-licensing
MIT claimed but not explicitly documented

abandoned_unmaintained.reason: Last commit >12 months ago; unclear if functional with current LLM APIs; likely broken
examples: Pre-Claude-3.5 agents (May not work with current Claude API)
GPT-3.5-only agents (functionality may be outdated)
Inactive repositories (no responses to issues, no recent commits)

key_insights.rarity_of_reusable_infrastructure: Most AI agent projects are either domain-specific, experimental, or single-task. True reusable infrastructure (orchestration, security, persistence) is rare.
key_insights.quality_bar: The 5 projects that cleared our quality bar (Citadel, Agent Memory Guard, Lead Score Flow, GenAI_Agents, PII Sanitizer) represent the top ~1% of the 500-agent collection.
key_insights.production_readiness_gap: Gap between 'working example' and 'production-grade infrastructure' is significant. Most OSS agents are not designed for multi-tenant, autonomous, production use.
key_insights.licensing_clarity: Licensing is often ambiguous in agent projects, especially in example collections. Always verify before code reuse.

recommendation: The rejection of 99% of candidates validates our selection of the 5 shortlisted projects. Do not broaden the net. Focus on deep integration of Citadel, Agent Memory Guard, and Lead Score Flow.
